page: Amazon Web Services m8azn.metal-24xl is a bare-metal general-purpose instance powered by a dedicated 96-core AMD EPYC 9R05 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with a single thread per core and running at clock speeds up to 5.0 GHz, the platform provides direct access to 96 physical execution cores without virtualization overhead. Memory provisioning includes 384.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 system memory operating at 6 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes 200 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. No local storage disks and no hardware GPUs are bundled with this configuration, requiring attached Elastic Block Store volumes for persistent storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier execution across computing, memory, and networking domains. Single-core performance registers a Geekbench score of 3133.0 and a stress-ng rating of 4219.78, complemented by a multi-core Geekbench score of 31392.0 and PassMark CPU score of 167444.75. The 6 GHz DDR5 memory subsystem yields high bandwidth, achieving 1059.86 GB/sec in large-block uncached reads and 400.32 GB/sec in large-block writes. Microbenchmarks further show high throughput, with static web serving reaching 152.9 GB/sec and Redis SET performance measuring 334.99 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency standpoint, the bare-metal architecture maximizes resource yield by eliminating hypervisor contention and licensing overheads. While the lack of bundled local NVMe storage requires external network-attached volumes, the combination of 96 high-frequency cores, 200 Gbps network connectivity, and dense DDR5 memory offers efficient scale for compute-intensive enterprise applications. The platform is well suited for memory-resident caching, high-throughput web architectures, large software compilation pipelines, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services m8azn.metal-24xl is a bare-metal, general-purpose server powered by a 96-core AMD EPYC 9R05 processor on the x86_64 architecture operating at up to 5.0 GHz. Designed with dedicated physical cores and one thread per core, the system bypasses virtualization overhead. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of 6 GHz DDR5 RAM (4.0 GB per core) and a 200 Gbps baseline network interface. No local physical storage or GPUs are included. Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the top tier across computing, memory throughput, and networking, highlighted by a multi-core Geekbench score of 31392.0 and 1059.86 GB/sec large-block uncached read bandwidth. Given its non-virtualized core density and rapid memory architecture, the instance fits high-concurrency enterprise workloads, software compilation, Redis in-memory databases, and large-scale web serving tiers.
